sentences.text:
This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellants - owners of the offending vehicle challenging the judgment and award dated 16th September, 2014 passed in MVC No.130/2010 on the file of the IX Additional Small Causes Judge & XXXIV ACMM, Court of Small Causes and Member, MACT-7, Bengaluru (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity).
2.

entities.text: Additional Small Causes Judge & XXXIV ACMM, Court of Small Causes and Member, MACT-7, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The deceased died in the accident.
Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation by fastening liability on the appellants/owners of the offending vehicle - tempo on the ground that as on the date of the accident, there was no insurance coverage.
In the present case, the appellants/owners of the offending vehicle questioned the liability fixed on them to pay the compensation.

3. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.
NC: 2024:KHC:21382 4.

Learned counsel for the appellants/owners submitted that the accident caused on 6.5.2009 and the insurance coverage was for the period from 14.8.2008 to 13.8.2009 and therefore, as on the date of the accident, there was valid insurance coverage.
Hence prays to fix liability on the insurance company to pay the compensation by indemnifying the appellants/owners.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent - insurance company submits that Ex.R1/insurance policy is valid for the period from 14.8.2009 to 13.8.2010.
Therefore, there was no insurance coverage.
Hence, the Tribunal is justified in passing the impugned judgment and award fastening liability on the appellants - owners of the offending vehicle.
6. Before the Tribunal, the insurance company has produced insurance policy - Ex.R1.

As per Ex.R1,
the insurance policy is valid for the period from 14.8.2009 to 13.8.2010.
7. In this appeal, the appellants/owners have filed copy of the insurance policy as additional evidence by invoking the provisions of Order - XLI Rule 27 of the Code Civil Procedure.
The additional document of the insurance policy is produced NC: 2024:KHC:21382 with the prayer to consider the same as an additional evidence.
The said insurance policy is valid for the period from 14.8.2008 to 13.8.2009.
The appellants want to produce additional evidence to prove that there was valid insurance coverage as on the date of the accident.
But the insurance policy produced is the copy of the insurance policy, but not the original or certified copy.

However, it is contended that the appellants/owners have evidence to prove that there was valid insurance coverage as on the date of accident and prays to remand the case to the Tribunal so as to enable the appellants to produce evidence before the Tribunal proving insurance coverage.
Whether there was insurance coverage or not as on the date of accident is a disputed fact to be adjudicated before the Tribunal upon receiving evidence in this regard.

Therefore reserving liberty to the appellants to prove the above said aspects,
the case is required to be remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC:21382 ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 16th September, 2014 passed in MVC.No.130/2010, on the file of the IX Additional Small Causes Judge & XXXIV ACMM, Court of Small Causes and Member, MACT-7, Bengaluru, is hereby set-aside.
iii) The matter is remanded back to the jurisdictional tribunal.

sentences.text: The Tribunal shall consider the material placed before this Court and any other relevant material that would be placed by the parties before it in respect of fastening liability, by providing reasonable opportunity to both parties to adduce further evidence in respect of their respective cases and decide the matter afresh, in accordance with law.
iv) Parties along with their respective counsel are directed to appear before the jurisdictional tribunal on 15th July 2024 without awaiting any further notice either from the tribunal or this Court.
The Tribunal shall decide the matter within a period of nine months thereafter.
v) Parties shall cooperate for early disposal of the matter.
vi) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy NC: 2024:KHC:21382 of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
vii) It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion with regard to merits of the matter.
viii) All contentions of both parties are kept open.
